sources.note: Nothing on stress; documents that no description exists. Table 1 (p.181): Tofanma data = 'ca 250 words and 15 sentences'. sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 2007. Australasia and the Pacific. In Christopher Moseley (ed.), Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages, 425-577. London: Routledge. [entry 'Tofamna [367]', p.543; cross-reference to the 'Damal' entry for TNGP structural type]
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No language-specific prosodic statement. Verbatim: 'P, TNGP, Tofamna. Little is known about its structure, but what is known, agrees with the TNGP type (see the Damal entry) in general.' The Damal entry's generic TNGP profile says 'Main structural features of TNGP languages are the presence of phonologically relevant tones in many of them, complicated verb morphology.' -- a family-type generalisation ('in many of them'), not an observation about Tofamna, whose total documentation is ~250 words; not usable as a tone or stress statement for this languoid.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, Vol. 1: Papuan Languages and the New Guinea Linguistic Scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 345-459. Canberra: ANU. [Tofamna: sec. 2.6.2.2.17 'Sub-phylum-level isolates', p.423]
sources.note: Nothing for Tofamna. p.423: 'There are still four languages within the TNGP which on the basis of our present knowledge cannot be included in any of the known stocks. Very little is known of these languages, and at present little more can be done than enumerate them. They are: Molof. Usku. Tofamna. Word lists in these three languages have been published in Voorhoeve 1971. Morwap.' The phoneme inventory and nasalisation note that follows concerns Morwap only; the 'non-tonal; stress is phonemic' line on p.422 belongs to Nimboran (sec. 2.6.2.2.15).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. Dutton et al., Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing for Tofamna. Sec. 2.7 'Unclassified languages' (p.77, p.31): 'They are Molof (200 speakers), Usku (20 speakers) and Tofamna (number of speakers unknown).. The only data available is the wordlists collected by Galis (1956b).' Only cognate percentages and a comparative wordlist (Appendix I) are given; phonology/stress notes exist in this paper only for other languages (Sko, Morwap, Dara).

sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. Full text: location, neighbouring languages, and 'Berdasarkan hasil penghitungan dialektometri, isolek Tefanma merupakan sebuah bahasa dengan persentase perbedaan berkisar 98,50%--98,75% jika dibandingkan dengan bahasa di sekitarnya, misalnya bahasa Molof dan Yafi.' Implies an underlying Badan Bahasa 400-item wordlist for 'Tefanma' exists (unpublished).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. Namla-Tofanma. New Guinea World website (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch), page 'under construction'.
sources.note: No prosodic statement; historical-phonology cognate tables only. Source list names Galis 1956, Voorhoeve 1971/1975, Anceaux (Smits & Voorhoeve 1994, after Mallo), Menanti 2005 (245 terms, Tefalma = Tofanma I village) and Wambaliau 2005:24-27. The Menanti/Wambaliau transcriptions carry sporadic IPA stress marks (e.g. Tofanma 'urine' [ˈtʊ], 'child' [ˈmlɛ ~ məlɛ]) but most items are unmarked, so no placement rule can be read off.
